subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Anchorages: Where the Cable Meets the Earth
description: A quick, practical guide to Anchorages: Where the Cable Meets the Earth.

hook.text: The Golden Gate's cables pull on their anchorages with 63 million pounds of force. Something has to hold.

buildup.text: Anchorages are massive concrete blocks buried deep in rock. They absorb all the cable tension.

discovery.text: Each anchorage weighs tens of thousands of tons. Their mass alone keeps the cables from pulling free.

twist.text: Some bridges use gravity anchorages on land. Others drill cables into bedrock when there's no room for mass.

climax.text: Without anchorages, the cables would rip free and the entire bridge would snap like a rubber band.

punchline.text: The cables are beautiful. The anchorages do the work.

quiz.question: What is the primary function of anchorages on a suspension bridge?
options: They support the weight of the towers during construction
They absorb the massive pulling force from the main cables
They prevent the bridge deck from swaying in the wind
